{{Short description|Dutch physicist}}
[[File:Stan Bentvelsen.jpg|thumb|Stan Bentvelsen]]
'''Stan C.M. Bentvelsen''' (born 1965) is a Dutch [[Particle physics|experimental particle physicist]] and Professor of [[Large Hadron Collider|Large Hadron Collider Physics]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. He served as director of the Dutch National Institute for Subatomic Physics ([[Nikhef]]) from 2014 to 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uva.nl/en/shared-content/faculteiten/en/faculteit-der-natuurwetenschappen-wiskunde-en-informatica/news/2014/08/stan-bentvelsen-new-director-of-nikhef.html|title=Stan Bentvelsen new director of Nikhef - University of Amsterdam|first=Universiteit van|last=Amsterdam|website=www.uva.nl|accessdate=25 May 2018|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180525210809/http://www.uva.nl/en/shared-content/faculteiten/en/faculteit-der-natuurwetenschappen-wiskunde-en-informatica/news/2014/08/stan-bentvelsen-new-director-of-nikhef.html|archivedate=25 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/news/jorgen-dhondt-appointed-director-nikhef/|title=Jorgen D'Hondt appointed director Nikhef}}</ref> His scientific career has focused on experimental [[Particle physics|high-energy physics]], from studies of the internal structure of the proton to precision tests of the [[Standard Model]] and the physics of the [[Large Hadron Collider]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-11-26 |title=What is CERN all about |url=https://www.utoday.nl/news/62249/What_is_CERN_all_about |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=www.utoday.nl |language=en}}</ref> He has been closely involved in the [[ATLAS experiment]] at [[CERN]] since its preparatory phase and served as programme leader for the Dutch ATLAS physics programme from 2004 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=10 years Higgs: interview with Stan Bentvelsen |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/10-years-higgs-interview-with-stan-bentvelsen/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Nikhef |language=en-US}}</ref> In this role, he coordinated the Dutch scientific contribution during the period leading to the [[Search for the Higgs boson|discovery of the Higgs boson]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-08-16 |title=Who, what, where, when and why Higgs |url=https://higgsfilm.com/5-ws-about-higgs/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=Higgs |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
Bentvelsen began studying physics at the [[Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam]] in 1983. After completing his first year, he spent a year studying [[philosophy]] at the [[University of Amsterdam]] before continuing his studies in theoretical physics there. He graduated in 1989, with graduation research on cosmological scalar fields. He subsequently moved into experimental particle physics for his doctoral research at the University of Amsterdam, conducting his research with the [[ZEUS (particle detector)|ZEUS]] experiment at [[DESY]] in [[Hamburg]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Measurement of the proton structure function at HERA using the ZEUS detector |url=https://inspirehep.net/literature/373027 |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> He received his PhD cum laude from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Amsterdam |first=Universiteit van |date=2026-06-25 |title=Prof. dr. S.C.M. (Stan) Bentvelsen |url=https://www.uva.nl/en/profile/b/e/s.c.m.bentvelsen/s.c.m.bentvelsen.html |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=University of Amsterdam |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Bentvelsen's early research focused on the internal structure of the [[proton]]. As a member of the [[ZEUS (particle detector)|ZEUS]] collaboration at DESY, he participated in the first physics programme of the [[HERA (particle accelerator)|HERA]] electron-proton collider, using deep inelastic scattering to study the quark and gluon structure of the proton. During this period, he developed the double-angle method, a technique for reconstructing the [[kinematics]] of deep inelastic scattering events from angular measurements. The method was used in measurements of proton structure functions at HERA.<ref name=":0" />

After completing his doctorate, Bentvelsen joined [[CERN]], where he worked on the [[OPAL experiment]] at the [[Large Electron-Positron Collider]] (LEP).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bentvelsen Stan |url=https://www.bsbf2024.org/chair-speaker/bentvelsen-stan/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=BSBF 2024 - Big Science Business Forum 2024 in Trieste (Italy) |language=en-US}}</ref> His research included studies of [[quantum chromodynamics]] and precision measurements of [[Electroweak interaction|electroweak interactions]]. Towards the end of his time at [[CERN]], he joined the [[ATLAS experiment]], contributing to preparations for the physics programme of the Large Hadron Collider.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Stan Bentvelsen |url=https://www.ukri.org/people/stan-bentvelsen/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

After returning to the Netherlands in 2000, Bentvelsen continued his research with the ATLAS experiment at [[Nikhef]] and the University of Amsterdam. His research focused on the physics of proton-proton collisions at the LHC and on tests of the Standard Model. From 2004 to 2013, he served as programme leader for the Dutch ATLAS physics programme, coordinating the scientific activities of the Dutch groups during the commissioning and first years of operation of the LHC. This period included the ATLAS searches for the Higgs boson and its discovery in 2012.<ref>[http://www.nikhef.nl/pub/services/biblio/theses_pdf/thesis_S_Bentvelsen.pdf PDF bij Nikhef] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605120048/http://www.nikhef.nl/pub/services/biblio/theses_pdf/thesis_S_Bentvelsen.pdf |date=2013-06-05 }} S.C.M. Bentvelsen: ''Measurement of the proton structure function at HERA using the ZEUS detector'', Amsterdam, 1989.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nikhef.nl/over-nikhef/organisatie/directorate/|title=Directorate|website=www.nikhef.nl|accessdate=25 May 2018|url-status=live|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180525210808/https://www.nikhef.nl/over-nikhef/organisatie/directorate/|archivedate=25 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=INSPIRE: Stan Bentvelsen—author profile|url=https://inspirehep.net/authors/1016713|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-01-18|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref>

== Career ==
Bentvelsen joined [[CERN]] in 1994 as a research fellow and became a staff scientist in 1996. In 2000 he returned to the Netherlands to take up a senior research position at [[Nikhef]]. In 2004 he was appointed Professor of Large Hadron Collider Physics at the [[University of Amsterdam]], where he also served as director of the Institute of High Energy Physics from 2004 to 2014.

Bentvelsen became director of Nikhef in December 2014 and served two five-year terms, until 2024. As director, he was responsible for the scientific strategy and overall management of the institute and the Nikhef partnership with Dutch universities.<ref>{{Cite news |last=cern |date=2020-01-10 |title=Nikhef reappoints Bentvelsen – CERN Courier |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/nikhef-reappoints-bentvelsen/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |work=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref> During his tenure, the [[University of Groningen]] and [[Maastricht University]] joined the partnership, extending the national collaboration in particle and astroparticle physics.<ref name="nikhef ligo virgo">{{Cite web |title=LIGO and Virgo make first detection of gravitational waves produced by colliding neutron stars |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/news/ligo-and-virgo-make-first-detection-of-gravitational-waves-produced-by-colliding-neutron-stars/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Nikhef |language=en-US}}</ref> Alongside Nikhef's continuing involvement in [[CERN]]'s collider programme, the institute further developed its activities in areas including neutrino physics, dark matter searches and gravitational-wave science.

During his directorship of Nikhef, Bentvelsen became increasingly involved in gravitational-wave science. Following the first direct detection of gravitational waves in 2015,<ref name="nikhef ligo virgo" /> Nikhef expanded its activities in this field and joined the [[European Gravitational Observatory]] (EGO) and [[Virgo interferometer|Virgo]] collaboration in 2019. Together with [[Maastricht University]] and regional partners, Nikhef also became involved in preparations for the [[Einstein Telescope]], including the establishment of the ETpathfinder research facility in Maastricht.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plan to build Einstein Telescope submitted for European research roadmap |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/news/plan-to-build-einstein-telescope-submitted-for-european-research-roadmap/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Nikhef |language=en-US}}</ref>

Bentvelsen subsequently became involved in the European and Dutch preparations for the [[Einstein Telescope]]. Following its inclusion on the ESFRI Roadmap in 2021, the Netherlands established a national programme to investigate the feasibility of hosting the observatory in the [[Euregio Meuse-Rhine]]. In 2022, Bentvelsen helped establish the Einstein Telescope EMR Project Office, where he served as scientific director.<ref>{{Cite web |last=cern |date=2022-06-30 |title=Limbering up for the Einstein Telescope |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/limbering-up-for-the-einstein-telescope/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref> In February 2025, he was appointed Chief Science Officer (CSO) of Einstein Telescope Netherlands (ET-NL), with responsibility for the scientific part of the bid book for the Einstein Telescope.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dutch pledge nearly $1 billion to support underground gravitational wave detector |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/dutch-pledge-nearly-billion-to-support-underground-wave-detector |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=www.science.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Oud-Kamerlid Sjoerd Sjoerdsma aangesteld om Einstein Telescoop binnen te halen |url=https://www.v-dg.nl/J4SMWxCV |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=www.v-dg.nl |language=nl}}</ref>

== Recognition and advisory roles ==
In 2013, Bentvelsen and former Nikhef director Frank Linde jointly received the Physica Prize of the [[Netherlands Physical Society]] (NNV) for their contributions to the discovery of the Higgs boson with the ATLAS experiment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stan Bentvelsen herbenoemd als directeur Nikhef / Stan Bentvelsen reappointed as director Nikhef |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/news/stan-bentvelsen-herbenoemd-als-directeur-nikhef/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Nikhef |language=nl-NL}}</ref> In 2025, Bentvelsen was appointed a member of the Council of the UK Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Council members |url=https://www.ukri.org/who-we-are/how-we-are-governed/council-members/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
Bentvelsen has also been active in communicating particle physics to a wider audience. He appeared with [[Peter Higgs]] in the documentary ''Higgs'' ''- into the heart of imagination'', which followed the Dutch research group at [[CERN]] during the preparations for the LHC and the search for the [[Higgs boson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Higgs, Into the Heart of Imagination |url=https://www.filmfestival.nl/en/film/higgs-into-the-heart-of-imagination |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Nederlands Film Festival |language=en}}</ref> In 2022, he co-authored the popular science book ''Het eiland dat Higgs heet'' with science writer Martijn van Calmthout.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cosmos book award for “Het Eiland dat Higgs heet" |url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/news/cosmos-boekenprijs-voor-het-eiland-dat-higgs-heet/ |access-date=2026-08-15 |website=Nikhef |language=en-US}}</ref>
